public_rationale: Menlo Ventures' December 9, 2025 announcement estimated 2025 enterprise generative AI spending at $37 billion, including $19 billion for applications [e4]. This enterprise estimate does not establish a comparable total for all paid generative AI demand in 2025 [e4]. It supplies no matched prices, recurring costs and customer responses showing whether demand disappears or persists at fully cost-covering prices [e4]. Neither the $65 billion figure nor the claim of universal subsidy dependence is settled by this evidence [e4].
limitations: The evidence covers enterprise spending, not the complete market asserted in the claim.
The estimate was published before year-end and is not an audited final-year total.
The claim supplies no accounting or aggregation basis for the $65 billion figure.
The evidence does not measure fully allocated recurring costs or demand responses to cost-covering prices.

statement.excerpt: I’m going to be as blunt as possible: every bit of AI demand — and barely $65 billion of it existed in 2025 — that exists only exists due to subsidies, and if these companies were to charge a sustainable rate, said demand would evaporate.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: barely $65 billion of it existed in 2025
if these companies were to charge a sustainable rate
our_interpretation: In this discussion of model subscriptions and applications, AI demand means paid demand for generative AI services. Including all semiconductor sales or established advertising systems would stretch the context.
The monetary component concerns realized 2025 customer spending or provider revenue, with a consistent boundary that avoids counting the same spending repeatedly through suppliers.
The causal assertion concerns demand existing at publication. The target interval includes 2025 and the period through March 31, 2026.
Subsidies means outside funding or cross-subsidies allowing prices below the full recurring cost of sustaining the service.
Evaporate means commercially meaningful demand would disappear at cost-covering prices, not merely grow more slowly.
The conditional phrase is assessed as a causal counterfactual. It is not converted into a dated forecast or treated as an observed industry-wide price increase.
Barely is approximate; I do not invent a numerical tolerance. The quotation identifies no accounting or aggregation basis.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes the approximate 2025 market size and demonstrates that all commercially meaningful demand depends on below-cost pricing and disappears when full recurring costs are charged.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A consistently measured 2025 market size clearly conflicts with the stated magnitude, or credible observed demand persists at demonstrably fully cost-covering prices for a meaningful service within the claimed market.

evidence.explanation: The study separates application spending from infrastructure and estimates enterprise spending using survey and market data. Its narrower market and absence of supplier-cost measurements prevent it from settling either the aggregate $65 billion assertion or universal subsidy dependence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A consistently bounded total of realized 2025 spending or revenue that avoids supplier-chain double counting, plus studies matching prices, full recurring costs and customer responses. Universal subsidy dependence requires evidence that commercially meaningful demand disappears at cost-covering prices. Meaningful demand persisting at verified cost-covering prices would contradict that assertion.
